problem: Goal-oriented VLN (REVERIE, SOON) datasets are small and human annotation is expensive, which limits navigator accuracy and generalization; existing speakers/pseudo-instruction generators produce low-quality instructions.
motivation: Finding a target object from a natural language description in unseen environments needs much more data than is annotated. Higher-quality pseudo-instructions that reference objects and environment can augment training data, and self-training with a quality filter can make the speaker itself better despite limited data.
key_idea: Train a referring expression speaker (RES) with an environment-and-object fusion module and transformer encoding to generate pseudo-instructions for paths to goal objects, improve it by self-training filtered by a contrastive trajectory-instruction matching scorer (TIMS), and integrate everything in a multi-stage training strategy.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so ablation evidence cannot be cited. The abstract claims that pseudo-instruction quality (via object-aware spatial representations and scorer-based selection of self-training samples) is what drives navigator gains, and that the modules assist one another under multi-stage training.
method: Referring Expression Speaker (RES): predicts descriptive instructions for a given path to a goal object, used to produce pseudo-instructions for data augmentation.
Environment-and-Object Fusion (EOF) module: derives spatial representations from input trajectories by fusing environment and object features, then encoded by several transformer layers.
Self-training: RES is trained further on its own generated pseudo labels to overcome the limited dataset.
Trajectory-Instruction Matching Scorer (TIMS): contrastive-learning network scoring trajectory-instruction match, used to selectively rehearse prior knowledge / filter pseudo labels.
Multi-stage training strategy: integrates RES, TIMS and the navigator so modules help one another.

setting.backbone: Transformer-based speaker (RES) + TIMS scorer + GVLN navigator (details not given in abstract)
setting.training_data: REVERIE and SOON training data plus pseudo-instructions generated by RES (scale not stated in abstract)
setting.observation: not stated in abstract (likely panoramic RGB with object features)
setting.action_space: not stated in abstract (likely discrete nav-graph viewpoints)

numbers_note: abstract only; the abstract gives only relative improvements over SOTA (REVERIE: SR +4.72, SPL +2.55, RGS +3.45; SOON: SR +4.58, SPL +3.75, RGS +3.14), not absolute values.
results: Compared with SOTA methods, improves SR, SPL and RGS by 4.72%, 2.55% and 3.45% on REVERIE, and by 4.58%, 3.75% and 3.14% on SOON. The specific strongest baseline is not named in the abstract.
limitations: Depends on pseudo-instruction quality from a speaker trained on small data; the scorer is needed to filter noise.
Evaluated only on REVERIE and SOON (simulated, no real robot).
